scope: 15 whole exclusions, all fields inspected; repeated identical scope boilerplate corrected per record. Component decisions do not certify integration.
additional_source_basis: 185 and 186 fully reread in the earlier 27-referral pass; all supplied pages also received the independent pre-draft source-first pass.

rows.review_disposition: Couthon opens the nonjuror issue on 175; Isnard advocates exile on 177. Personal weighting is optional here, but the legislative initiative and exclusionary argument belong to refractory-clergy policy. Their substantive roles elsewhere remain eligible.

177/180/185 provide personnel within a substantive ministerial crisis. Exclude only independent biographical detail: Narbonne’s military hopes, the replacement by warmongers and the dismissal crisis must remain accessible through the political and war-policy subjects.

175/186/192 use foreign testimony to explain emigration, the royal/constitutional crisis and mass volunteering. No conjectural personal headings are needed; retain the evidence and the 192 distinction between trained regular warfare and patriotic mass recruitment.

197 expressly identifies noble killers angered by Gustavus’s democratic despotism, who blamed Jacobinism to divert responsibility. Retain that irony and European fear under reception/regicide; the independent reviewer’s new evidence proposal must fulfill the parent route. No separate royal-assassination unit is required, and Jacobin guilt must not be asserted.

200/204/219 confirm quotations embodying natural-frontier policy, coalition expectation and hostile reception. Attribution alone need not create another unit, but each underlying policy or reaction is substantive; Pitt, Danton and other speakers have eligible developed treatment elsewhere.

197/203 compress campaign places and commanders, but 203 explicitly connects defeats and guillotined generals to paranoia and military caution. Exclude separate default microheadings only; retain those mechanisms and any distinct turning-point retrieval. Duration alone is not a sufficient threshold.

221 gives appearance as personal detail and says Buzot would soon become her lover. Correct temporal phrasing; retain the informal Roland meeting network and Mme Roland’s political polemic under Girondin organization.

221 makes Philippe-Égalité’s elevation an inference in factional accusations, not an established plan. Retain the allegation’s political purpose without endorsing it or requiring an independent asserted royalist plot subject.

241 states Wimpffen was royalist, but English pay only possible and his politics unknown to those seeking aid. Preserve that distinction within federalist coalition divisions; an independent espionage heading is unwarranted.

254/255/257 support symbolic punitive renaming, including half-hearted Marseilles renaming and Bordeaux city retaining its name while its department changed. Retain these distinctions as subordinate access and punishment symbolism; no separate unit for every name is required.

255 links suspicions of moderate Bordeaux repression to Tallien’s supposed personal influence. Separate Cabarrus biography is optional here; this does not exclude the political suspicion or her later Thermidor role.

254 uses anonymous testimony to convey physical destruction and the justification of revolutionary violence. Retain that evidence under Lyons and Revolutionary Army, without inventing personal identification.

277 identifies David as painter, committee member and festival organizer. Festival organization and political art are meaningful subject content; a separate personal unit is optional for this brief treatment, not forbidden by the fact this is a subject index.

281 uses Rowan’s observation to support execution speed, popular reaction and hostility to the wage maximum. The witness needs no independent biography, but the political-economic evidence must survive and cannot prove that wages alone explain popular passivity.

285 names Paine parenthetically among restored deputies. This specific reinstatement is adequately retrievable through Girondin rehabilitation; his independently developed earlier/later ideas and roles remain eligible.

proposed_whole_exclusions.label: Individual rhetorical quotations used only to voice larger policies

proposed_whole_exclusions.rationale: The speakers should not automatically become separate access points when the passage's independently useful information concerns war aims, coalition assumptions, occupation, or European reaction.
